title: Anti-Aging Drug Rapamycin Increases Muscle and Reduces Pain: New Results

However, an epidemic of poor lifestyle choices, along with the pollutants manufactured by modern society, perpetuate chronic conditions such as lung cancer, cardiovascular disease, and dementia. Thus, while we tend to live longer, many individuals tend to suffer from these chronic conditions, referred to as age-related diseases. Adding to a growing body of clinical evidence revealing rapamycin’s age-intervening effects on humans, scientists at AgelessRx have found that the drug increases lean mass and reduces pain in older women but not older men. Results from the WOMAC (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis) survey, which includes questions pertaining to pain, stiffness, and physical function, showed no significant changes. Determining the optimal dose of rapamycin will require further research. Science translational medicine, 10(449), eaaq1564.
